dashboard.firstTitle: Start by creating your first subject.
dashboard.firstDescription: Cortex learns an exam’s format from its past exams, then generates practice papers that closely match it. It all starts with a course: yours.

dashboard.firstStep2Description: Real previous exams from the course (PDF, HTML…).
dashboard.firstStep3Description: Exercise types, actual weighting and recurring traps.

dashboard.onboardingDescription: Cortex hasn’t analysed this course yet. Give it the past exams: it identifies exercise types and their exam weighting, then always tells you what to work on next.
dashboard.onboardingStep1Description: Add the course’s real final exams (PDF, HTML…).
dashboard.onboardingStep2Description: It identifies exercise types and their actual exam weighting.
dashboard.onboardingStep3Description: The forgetting curve reschedules each type for you.

originals.localNote: Your file stays on your computer: Cortex reads its text (and the pages of a past exam while preparing the course), then removes it from its servers within {hours} hours. Only the index is kept for search and your mock exams.
originals.premiumHint: to keep it in the cloud and access it anywhere.
originals.badgeTitle: Cortex keeps its index, not the file.
originals.freeCloudEnded: Free accounts no longer keep files in the cloud
originals.retention: Your {count, plural, one {# file already in the cloud stays there} other {# files already in the cloud stay there}} until {date}. Cortex will then keep only their index: your mock exams won’t change, and you can resend a file from your computer.

originals.backHint: You’re Premium: import this course’s folder again to put {replacement} in the cloud. Cortex recognises each file by its fingerprint, so its index won’t change.

localSource.title: File on your computer
localSource.description: Cortex keeps only its index: search and your mock exams work without the file.
localSource.notLocal: This file isn’t an original stored on your computer.
localSource.premiumHint: to keep your files in the cloud and open them anywhere, even on your phone. Premium means an active subscription or a credit purchase within the past year.
localSource.textOnly: This text was added from your assistant: there is no file. Cortex keeps its index, so nothing is lost.
localSource.unsupported: Open it from your computer: <path>{where}</path>{page}. This browser can’t let Cortex find it; desktop Chrome and Edge can.
localSource.pickHint: Choose this course’s folder on your computer once. Cortex will find this file and the next ones there. Nothing is uploaded; the search happens in your browser.
localSource.allowHint: Your browser is requesting access to the “{folder}” folder again.
localSource.openWithApp: Open this file type from your computer with its app.
localSource.changed: “{folder}” contains a {name} file (<path>{where}</path>), but it has changed since import. Open it from your computer, or add this new version as new course material.
localSource.missing: {name} isn’t in “{folder}” or its subfolders. Choose the folder containing it, or open it from your computer: <path>{where}</path>.
localSource.sentCloud: Received: it’s now in the cloud and you can open it anywhere.
localSource.sentLocal: Received. Run “Prepare course” within {hours} hours: Cortex will reread its pages, then remove it from its servers.
localSource.sendInterrupted: Upload interrupted. Check your connection, then try again.
localSource.sendLocalHint: Useful for a past exam: Cortex rereads its pages (format and exercises) while preparing the course, then removes it from its servers.
localSource.sendCloudHint: It will join the cloud, so you can open it from any device.

import.folderHint: Finals and midterms go into your past exams and determine the format. Slides, problem sets, Word documents and notes join the rest of the course materials. Each file can be up to 30 MB, within your account’s storage limit. ZIP files, Canvas exports (.imscc) and Moodle backups (.mbz) are unpacked in your browser, even when they contain another archive.
import.formatOffer: To align the mock exam with these past exams, Cortex rereads their format: exercise types, weighting and duration. “Prepare course” does this too.
import.prepareHint: Cortex reads your course materials, recognises the final exam format and organises the topics to work on.
